comments.author: @csurampower
comments.text:
The guy didn't even bring up all of the other expenses to make a bowling center functional. The lane oil machine is at least $25k, plus the constant cost of oil and maintenance. The ball return wheel and mechanism on the approach needs constant maintenance. All of the displays (one for each lane) plus the computers (one for every two lanes). Wood lanes get dented and uneven through play and need resurfacing every 1-2 years for roughly $1k-2k per lane. Synthetic will last longer but eventually will need replacement for $20k per lane.  The foul light mechanism can be difficult to repair depending upon their age and part availability. Rental shoes cost at least $100 per pair because the companies that sell them know you can't get them anywhere else. And on, and on.
The center I worked at years ago had over 1,000 league bowlers per week and it was packed every night, and we still basically broke even strictly on the bowling. The revenue mostly came from food and alcohol, vending, the pro shop, the arcade, and the sponsorship/advertising all over the building. I can totally see why bowling centers are struggling with the cost of everything skyrocketing (along with social shifts and other factors). Also, f*** private equity.
